clips.text: After you.
clips.script: [polite, dry] After you.

clips.text: hey babe. safe flight. the smog over 2nd ave turned purple this morning. it'll probably blow over.

clips.text: That oven is the size of our kitchen, and every flame on the block is inside it.
clips.script: [awed, plain] That oven is the size of our kitchen, [stunned] and every flame on the block is inside it.

clips.text: Those flames belong to the stoves on 2nd Avenue.
clips.script: [careful, firm] Those flames belong to the stoves on Second Avenue.

clips.text: We have dough.
clips.script: [plain, hopeful] We have dough.

clips.text: There's a gold coin on your door. I need it, and I have to tell you what it does before I take it.
clips.script: [respectful, careful] There's a gold coin on your door. [steady, honest] I need it, [serious] and I have to tell you what it does before I take it.

clips.text: It isn't your pension. It opens an orange block on our street. When it does, every flame goes home and you go back to being an oven. A cold one. You won't be able to talk.
clips.script: [gentle, honest] It isn't your pension. [steady] It opens an orange block on our street. [careful, plain] When it does, every flame goes home and you go back to being an oven. [quiet, sorry] A cold one. [soft] You won't be able to talk.

clips.text: No. It has a rosebush on it.
clips.script: [gentle, plain] No. [quiet, honest] It has a rosebush on it.

clips.text: Six o'clock.
clips.script: [plain, careful] Six o'clock.

clips.text: Thank you for the bread.
clips.script: [quiet, sincere] Thank you for the bread.

clips.text: It goes in the round hole. It's your rosebush, so it should be you.
clips.script: [warm, simple] It goes in the round hole. [steady, kind] It's your rosebush, so it should be YOU.

clips.text: It's going in my mother's junk drawer with the other seven.
clips.script: [polite, firm] It's going in my mother's junk drawer with the other seven.

clips.text: No comment.
clips.script: [prim, deadpan] No comment.

clips.text: Somebody always did.
clips.script: [dry, low, delighted] Somebody always did.

clips.text: An old-timer from the barn. He retired today.
clips.script: [gentle, plain] An old-timer from the barn. [quiet, warm] He retired today.

clips.text: I have to fly back tomorrow.
clips.script: [quiet, plain] I have to fly back tomorrow.

clips.text: That leaves you alone on this street with Bernadette.
clips.script: [concerned, dry] That leaves you alone on this street with Bernadette.

clips.text: Twenty years, one witness. That's a strong number one. What's number two?
clips.script: [serious, taking notes in his head] Twenty years, one witness. [sincere, impressed] That's a STRONG number one. [eager] What's number two?

clips.text: Hi, Mom. I missed yours too. Is that the cinnamon topping? I've been thinking about that topping since we flew over Kansas.
clips.script: [warm] Hi, Mom. I missed yours too. [sniffing, hopeful] Is that the cinnamon topping? [earnest confession] I've been thinking about that topping since we flew over KANSAS.

clips.text: GAH! I'm on the floor. Grace, is that your elbow or mine?
clips.script: [real yelp] GAH! [breathless, amazed] I'm on the floor. [polite, laughing at himself] Grace, is that your elbow or mine?
